s1.explanation: Responds to small ornate decorative accents on accessories, especially jewelry-like metalwork: gold or silver pieces with rhinestones or gems, bows, ribbons and flower-shaped ornaments, and dangling chains or cords. Activity is highest when one such ornamented object is shown clearly and close up, and lower in cluttered scenes or on plain, unornamented items. Compared with similar units, it prefers sparkling metallic or jeweled floral and bow ornaments (brooch, buckle, necklace, hair bow) over embroidered or knitted pattern textures (skull loafer, knitted mitten) and printed graphics (binder).

s2.explanation: The unit responds to ornamental, jewelry-like adornment. Its strongest responses are to gold or metal pieces with bows, flowers, rhinestones or gems: a bow brooch with earrings, a jeweled flower buckle, a gold leaf necklace and a butterfly hair slide. It also responds to pendants hanging on cords and to objects with decorative motifs worked into the surface, such as a snakeskin wallet with a metal plaque, embossed leather, and printed or appliquéd stockings. Activity is highest when one such decorated item is shown clearly as a product, often on a plain background. It is low for plain undecorated items and for cluttered scenes with many objects, such as a store rack of holsters. Compared with the similar units, it is particular to sparkly metal or gem jewelry and dangling ornaments rather than skulls, knit textures or printed graphics.

s3.explanation: The unit responds mainly to ornate jewelry-like ornamentation: shiny gold or silver metalwork set with rhinestones or gems, formed into bows, flowers or filigree. Examples are brooches, earring sets, a jeweled flower buckle and a gold necklace. It also responds, more weakly, to a decorative motif on an object's surface, such as a tooled or embossed leather design or a printed Santa. Activity is highest for a single item laid out as a product shot on a plain light background. It drops for cluttered scenes, items on hangers, and plain objects with no ornament. Compared with the similar units, it is particular in preferring sparkly metallic jewelry and gems over textile or knit patterns, embroidered motifs and printed graphics.

real_s1.explanation: The unit may weakly prefer small attached ornaments on accessories, such as bows, ribbons, flowers or sparkling metal and jewels, but none of the specific predictions held, so its selectivity within its top classes is unclear.

real_s2.explanation: The unit seems to respond most to decorative jewelry-like ornamentation, meaning metal or gem adornments such as brooches, buckles and necklaces. It responds more weakly to decorated surfaces on single product-style items.

real_s3.explanation: The unit seems to respond to ornate decorative ornamentation on an object, such as bows, flowers, filigree or embossed motifs, mostly when the item is shown alone as a product shot on a plain light background. It does not appear to prefer shiny metal or gems over other materials.

null_s1.explanation: The ornament description is not supported. The only notable signal is that, within its top classes, the unit is more active on cluttered scenes with many items than on single close-up objects against plain backgrounds, which is the opposite of what was predicted.

null_s2.explanation: The unit is most active on a set of 24 classes that seem to involve decorated accessories and adornment, but within those classes none of the proposed features (jewelry-like metal or gems, dangling ornaments, a single item on a plain background) predicts its activity.

null_s3.explanation: The unit responds to ornate or detailed decorative motifs on an object's surface, such as bows, flowers, tooled or embossed designs, or printed pictures, whatever the material. It does not specifically prefer shiny metal jewelry or clean product shots.
